novelty: Test whether one causally transferable state carries the bidirectional period-versus-question-mark decision across reporting-frame and direct-question constructions, while leaving reporter rewrites invariant and not transferring an explicit punctuation-copy task. This challenges a head-identity reading of the old question circuit; it does not claim a new circuit merely by rediscovering attention layer 10 or head 10.5.

Test whether one site carries which explicitly introduced person performed an action, expressed as the correct he-versus-she continuation, across independently worded active-voice and passive-voice constructions. The linked location rewrite must remain invariant, and the same site must not transfer an unrelated explicit pronoun-copy task with identical output tokens. This extends pronoun-class and gender-readout evidence to natural, answer-changing antecedent counterfactuals; rediscovering head 12.4 or MLP17 without A1/A2 transfer and control selectivity is not novel.

Test whether a full residual-site donor-to-recipient replacement transfers pending-quote state across both a simple quoted noun phrase and a construction containing an earlier balanced quote pair. The same site must preserve the answer under writer rewrites and must not transfer a natural sentence-end-versus-inch-mark completion with the identical period and quote-token endpoints. This is not a new closer-head discovery and does not revive the invalid legacy quote DAS result.

Replace the abandoned learned-coordinate localization compiler with direct donor interchange of the exact full residual or module-output state at the final prediction position across two syntactic constructions. The screen asks whether one common site transfers both prepositional-phrase and relative-clause subject number while remaining small for noun-identity and attractor-number controls. The reusable scorer now derives C from the frozen task declaration: because Task 14 C preserves the answer, it measures absolute patched-versus-native movement normalized by the median A1/A2 donor effect, under the existing C ceiling. This preserves Task 14 semantics and adds a reusable causal localization step. Finding only that the state is distributed or robust would reproduce sections 1550-1552 and is not novel; novelty would require selective cross-syntax interchange at a specific boundary or a well-supported null under this stronger counterfactual.
